# THEORYs with `tags` `compositionality`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Compositionality** — how the structure and meaning of a whole come from its parts and how they are combined — the principle of compositionality and compositional semantics, the emergence of compositional structure in languages under transmission, and composition and binding in learned models (generalization to unseen combinations, attribute binding, composing distributions or concepts). A work on making a model generalize compositionally is ML practice and goes to the anthology (ADR-031).

| [THEORY-117](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-117.md) v3 | In Uselis, Dittadi and Oh's two-concept grids, ResNet-50s trained from scratch, with checkpoints chosen on the unseen pairs, reach unseen combinations as the share of combinations seen grows and not as up to four times more data of the same combinations is added; and when embeddings are exactly linearly factored, seen pairs that connect every value of both concepts, as two per value arranged in one cycle do, determine the embedding of every unseen pair | Uselis, Dittadi & Oh (2025), [LIT-667](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-667.md). In an n × n grid of two concepts with k combinations seen per value, ResNet-50s trained from scratch fit seen pairs and fail on unseen ones; four times the data of the same combinations leaves 60–80% drops, while more values and more combinations help. Features pass from spurious, to decodable but entangled, to linearly factored as coverage grows. Model selection was on the test set, by design, so the results bound what is possible. The record re-derived that exactly factored embeddings of every unseen pair are fixed by seen pairs connecting every value, as the paper's k = 2 cycle does. Honest selection, other architectures and more concepts are [QUESTION-207](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-207.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-164](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-164.md) | In groups that build a new communication system, larger groups make it more systematic, and the greater variety of input they face drives the effect | Raviv, Meyer & Lev-Ari (2019), [LIT-825](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-825.md), read in [NOTE-628](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-628.md): fully connected groups of eight built more systematic languages than groups of four, faster and more uniformly, with total interaction and network structure fixed; input variability, larger in bigger groups, predicted the gains. One laboratory study, two group sizes, and a mechanism supported by lagged association, not manipulation. It says nothing yet about natural communities, where size travels with network density and second-language learners. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-167](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-167.md) v2 | The Russian wondertale is built from a small fixed set of character functions in a fixed order, so that all wondertales share one composition and differ in who performs the functions and how | Propp (1928), [LIT-828](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-828.md), read in [NOTE-615](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-615.md): in Afanasyev's tales 50–151 the constant elements are 31 functions of characters, defined by their consequence for the action, occurring in one order and falling to seven roles. | [THEORY-201](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-201.md) v2 | In next-token prediction on hierarchically generated sequences, the correlation between two tokens falls by about a factor m per level of their common ancestor, so a training set of P sequences resolves correlations only out to a distance t*(P) at which they meet sampling noise; learners come to represent the hidden symbols up to that depth, giving loss steps at about v m^(2ℓ−1) examples, and on character-level text the context at which the loss saturates grows as P^(1/(2β)) with β the measured correlation decay | Cagnetta and Wyart (2024), [LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md), extending [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md) from labels to masked tokens: the correlation plateaus and the noise floor are derived for the Random Hierarchy Model in the large-v, large-m limit; the loss steps and the representation probes are measured in small transformers and CNNs; the link between them is argued, not proved; and the real-text evidence, from two character-level corpora, tests the effective context window, not the hierarchy. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-519](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-519.md) | Supervised learners compose only once each carries a request function that passes a corrected input upstream; with it they form a symmetric monoidal category, and for a fixed step size and an error whose derivative in its first argument is invertible, gradient descent with backpropagation is a faithful strong symmetric monoidal functor into it from differentiable parametrised functions | Fong, Spivak & Tuyéras (2017; LICS 2019), [LIT-827](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-827.md), read in full in [NOTE-625](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-625.md), which followed the chain-rule proof of Theorem A.1 line by line. Learners (P, I, U, r) form Learn (Prop. II.4); Theorem III.2 makes gradient descent with backpropagation a functor Para → Learn. | [THEORY-686](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-686.md) v2 | An observation modelled as a monotone map between preorders can show of a joined system more than the join of its observations of the parts, and out of a preorder with all joins the observations that preserve all joins, the empty join and infinite joins included, are exactly the left adjoints | Fong & Spivak (2018), [LIT-803](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-803.md), Chapter 1, read closely in a Skimmed NOTE ([NOTE-601](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-601.md)) whose other chapters were seen only at their openings.
